_rule: A MODELLED company, not a client. Every number in this file is an assumption, labelled as one, and every one can be changed on the page. Measured figures come from evidence/fallfloor.json; prices, wages, inflation and statutes from sources/.
name: A modelled UK digital bank with EU customers

profile.footprint: Head office in the UK; customers in the UK and the EU — so UK GDPR, EU GDPR (Art 3(2)) and, where AI output is used in the EU, the EU AI Act (Art 2(1)(c)) all apply.

growth.why: Volume growth per year for the work (tickets, messages, questions, documents); seats are held flat.

hardware.why: Both sides run on the same laptops the company already owns — Copilot runs on them on the corporate side, the open models run on them here. No new hardware is bought on either side, so hardware cancels out.

nodeShare.why: A quarter of laptops enrolled as AI nodes — on mains power, managed by device policy.

hoursPerDay.why: Node hours per working day while the laptop is on and plugged in.

watts.why: The extra draw of AI work on a laptop that is already on: the chip's rated sustained power (Intel Processor Base Power).

model.name: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (Apache 2.0) — the model fallfloor measured on this hardware

workloads.name: Customer support: route, topic and a draft reply citing the help article, for the agent to approve
workloads.savedWhy: Reading the ticket, choosing the team and topic, and drafting the reply — one minute is the floor even with Copilot open; the agent's approval stays on both sides and is not counted.

workloads.name: Inbound message screening: suspected spam and scams flagged for a person
workloads.savedWhy: Ten seconds to read a message and decide. Messages the model flags still go to a person, so only the share it clears counts (measured in fallfloor).

workloads.name: Staff HR helpdesk: route each question to the right HR topic
workloads.savedWhy: Reading a staff question and routing it to the right HR topic.

workloads.name: KYC document field extraction, confirmed by an analyst
workloads.savedWhy: Keying the fields from an identity or address document; the analyst's confirmation stays on both sides and is not counted.
workloads.why: Tokens are an estimate (a document's text in, the fields out). Not biometric identification.

workloads.name: Internal knowledge assistant for staff (answers from the bank's own documents)
workloads.savedWhy: Not counted: Copilot seats give staff an assistant too, so this is where the two sides are like for like.
workloads.why: 1,000 knowledge workers × 10 questions a working day × 21 days. Tokens are an estimate (retrieved passages in, a short answer out).

outOfScope.name: Credit decisions
outOfScope.why: High-risk under AI Act Annex III 5(b) from 2 December 2027, a fundamental rights impact assessment (Art 27) and GDPR Art 22 / UK Arts 22A–22D. Not in this rollout; the gate shows why.

hoursPerFte.why: Productive hours a month per full-time person, used only to express the hours as people.

staffTime.why: The work the AI takes over, in seconds per item (floor-level: the least a person spends even with Copilot's help), priced at the National Living Wage.

onCost.why: Employer's National Insurance, pension and overheads on top of pay — an estimate; change it.

local.role: AI platform engineers (models, the floor, receipts)
Data protection and AI governance (with the DPO)

cloud.role: Data protection and AI governance (with the DPO)

staff.why: The same size of team on both sides (3 FTE). Salaries are ONS medians (sources/prices.json).

dayRate.why: Blended cost of a day of legal / privacy specialist time — an assumption; change it.

local.why: DPIAs per workload, AI system register, AI literacy plan, Article 50 notices, supply-chain and device security reviews.

cloud.why: The same, plus processor due diligence and contracts for each AI vendor, transfer risk assessments, and yearly vendor reviews.

policy._what: The go/no-go thresholds this design proposes to the CTO. They are choices, not facts, and the page lets you change them.

sensitivity._rule: What a CFO will push on. Each scenario changes one or more levers and re-runs the whole plan through the kernel. A lever is a number (an assumption, labelled) or a figure in sources/prices.json (named by its path, so it keeps its source).

scenarios.label: Staff time saved per item halved
scenarios.why: People spend half the floor-level seconds assumed on each item.

scenarios.label: People's time at the ONS median hourly wage, not the National Living Wage
Inflation at the Bank of England's target
Volumes flat — no growth at all
Laptops drawing their maximum turbo power the whole time
scenarios.why: Intel's Maximum Turbo Power for the chip.

scenarios.label: The owned apps take over a year later
scenarios.why: Two years of rent on both sides before the organs take over.

scenarios.label: Hardening the owned apps takes twice as long
scenarios.why: Double the engineering days for every organ and for the shared records.

scenarios.label: Every downside at once: time halved, inflation at target, volumes flat, laptops at maximum power, the owned apps a year late and twice the hardening
scenarios.why: The six levers that shrink the saving, together.

saas.why: The back office the bank rents per seat, where an estate organ covers the function. Prices from fallstack's registry; the organ and its rung on the ladder from fallstack's organ map and GitHub's record. Seat counts are floor-level assumptions; the functions no organ replaces (ticketing, e-signature, payroll) are left out of both sides.

cutoverYear.why: Year 1 runs both: the rent is still paid while each organ is hardened and the records move; the organ takes over from year 2.

hardeningDays.why: Engineering days to harden one organ for a 1,200-person bank — its named gaps, single sign-on, the bank's connectors, the migration — fewer for an organ further up the ladder. At the compliance day rate.

syncDays.why: Once, for all the replaced apps: the estate apps keep each browser's records locally today, so a shared, signed record across a team is built on the company's own mesh.

stack.why: Sales, relationship and marketing staff: about one in ten of the bank's people, on the cheapest paid Salesforce suite above the small-team Starter.
The finance team's full users, on the Microsoft ERP a Microsoft 365 bank would buy.
The HR team's full users; employee self-service not counted.
